'''''Rubus odoratus''''', the '''purple-flowered raspberry''',<ref name="fnwe">{{Cite web |last=Stace |first=Clive |author-link=Clive A. Stace |editor-last=van der Meijden |editor-first=Ruud |editor2-last=de Kort |editor2-first=Ingrid |title=Flora of NW Europe > Species: Rubus odoratus (Raspberry, purple-flowered) |url=http://wbd.etibioinformatics.nl/bis/flora.php?selected=beschrijving&menuentry=soorten&id=2607 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131111174607/http://wbd.etibioinformatics.nl/bis/flora.php?selected=beschrijving&menuentry=soorten&id=2607 |archive-date=2013-11-11 |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=Etibioinformatics.nl}}</ref><ref name=GRIN>{{GRIN | accessdate = 12 January 2018}}</ref> '''flowering raspberry''',<ref name=GRIN /> or '''Virginia raspberry''', is a species of ''[[Rubus]]'' native to eastern North America. It is sometimes referred to as '''thimbleberry''',<ref>{{cite web|title=''Rubus odoratus'' — flowering raspberry|url=https://gobotany.nativeplanttrust.org/species/rubus/odoratus/|website=Native Plant Trust}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=''Rubus odoratus'' {{!}} flowering raspberry|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/16141/rubus-odoratus/details|website=RHS}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=''Rubus odoratus''|url=https://www.wildflower.org/plants/result.php?id_plant=RUOD|website=Plant Database|publisher=University of Texas}}</ref> a name more commonly associated with the North American ''[[Rubus parviflorus|R. parviflorus]]''.

== Description ==
''Rubus odoratus'' is a [[shrub]] growing to {{convert|3|m|ft|0}} tall,<ref name="fnwe" /> with [[perennial]], not [[biennial plant|biennial]], stems (unlike many other species in the genus). Also, unlike most related species, this plant does not have thorns.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|series=Wildflowers of the Southeastern United States |url=http://2bnthewild.com/plants/H47.htm |title=''Rubus odoratus''|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927225736/http://2bnthewild.com/plants/H47.htm |archive-date=2007-09-27|date=2001-07-20}}</ref> The [[leaves]] are palmately lobed with five (rarely three or seven) lobes, up to {{Convert|25|cm|frac=2}} across, superficially resembling maple leaves.<ref name=":0" />

The [[flower]]s are {{Convert|3-5|cm|abbr=on|frac=2}} in diameter,<ref name="fnwe" /> with five magenta or occasionally white [[petal]]s; they are produced from early summer to early fall.<ref name=":0" /> Maturing in late summer to early autumn, the red edible [[fruit]] resembles a large, flat [[raspberry]]<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1">{{cite book | author=Blanchan | title=Wild Flowers Worth Knowing | year=1917 | publisher=[[Project Gutenberg]] Literary Archive Foundation| author-link=Neltje Blanchan |url=https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/8866/pg8866-images.html|first=Neltje|last2=Dickinson|first2=Asa Don}}</ref> with 30–60 [[drupe]]lets,<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Rubus odoratus in Flora of North America |url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=250100440 |access-date=2026-06-15 |website=eFloras.org}}</ref> and feels rather fuzzy.

== Distribution and habitat ==
The species is native to eastern North America, from [[Nova Scotia]] west to [[Ontario]] and [[Wisconsin]], and south along the [[Appalachian Mountains]] as far as [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] and [[Alabama]].<ref name="GRIN" /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Rubus%20odoratus.png|title=Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map|publisher=}}</ref> It is locally [[naturalisation (biology)|naturalized]] in parts of Washington state,<ref>{{cite web|website=USDA Plants Profile |url=https://plants.usda.gov/home/plantProfile?symbol=RUOD |title=''Rubus odoratus''}}</ref> Vermont, and also in Europe, notably southeastern England.<ref name="fnwe" />

It prefers partial shade,<ref name=":1" /> moisture,<ref name=":2" /> and rich, slightly [[acidic soil]].

== Uses ==
''Rubus odoratus'' is grown as an [[ornamental plant]]<ref name="fnwe" /> for its conspicuous flowers and long flowering period.

The fruits may be edible, but are dry and flavorless.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" />
